name: Amapiano
summary: South African house hybrid built on a tuned, syncopated log-drum bassline, a continuous shaker that acts as the real timekeeper, and a deliberately sparse, understated kick. This library approximates the log drum's RHYTHM only (tomLow+congaLow) - the genuine pitched instrument is a synth/bass part outside this drum-only kit's reach.

sounds.kick: Soft, rounded, house-adjacent kick reduced to one or two hits a bar so it never competes with the log drum's low end; a tighter kick suits the Bacardi/underground lane.
sounds.snare: Rarely used as such - rimshots and claps (rim/perc slots) supply syncopated backbeat answers, often a Kwaito-descended clave-adjacent conga shape rather than a straight 2-and-4.
sounds.hats: Sparse, mostly offbeat accents kept well under the shaker in the mix - the shaker, not the hat, is the genre's running 16th engine.
sounds.percussion: tomLow+congaLow approximate the log drum's rhythm (NOT its pitched bass tone); a continuous, velocity-contoured shaker is the true timekeeper; congas/rimshots/claps layer syncopated call-and-response on top.
sounds.cymbals: Essentially absent - tension is built through the piano/log-drum interplay, not cymbal energy; a ride, when used at all, sits far back and low in a breakdown.

machines: LinnDrum / Oberheim DMX - soft house-adjacent kick for the Private School lane
Roland TR-909 - tighter kick for the Bacardi/underground lane; hats
Roland TR-727 - synthesized conga, clave, cowbell and shaker patches
Roland CR-78 - softer analogue conga/bongo tones for the Private School lane
Roland TR-808 - pitched-down low tom as the log-drum rhythm reference
E-mu SP-1200 - lo-fi resample for the log-drum attack reference
Korg KR-55 / KPR-77 - period-adjacent latin percussion rims and shakers
A tuned synth/sampled log-drum patch and real congas/shakers - the genuine pitched log drum and live hand percussion this drum-only library cannot reproduce
references: Kabza De Small & DJ Maphorisa - Scorpion Kings sessions
